blocks.content: Metamorphic rocks are formed through the alteration of pre-existing parent rocks under extreme heat and pressure.

items: Direct matching questions between Parent Rock and Metamorphic Rock (e.g., Granite to Gneiss, Limestone to Marble) are highly frequent in competitive exams.
Quartzite is derived from Sandstone, whereas Slate and Schist originate from Shale and Clay.
Coal serves as an organic sedimentary parent rock that metamorphoses into Anthracite, Graphite, and Diamond.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Metamorphic rocks originate from pre-existing igneous or sedimentary parent rocks subjected to intense heat and pressure.
Thermal metamorphism is driven primarily by intense heat, while dynamic metamorphism is driven by intense pressure.
Granite acts as the parent rock for Gneiss through high-grade regional metamorphism.
Limestone recrystallizes into Marble, creating a fine-grained non-foliated rock.
Sandstone transforms into highly durable Quartzite under extreme pressure and heat.
